title: Long sessions, and Autrey quietly signalling Fats about weak takes
summary: Four-hour sessions ran over; Autrey shook his head or took Fats aside during breaks to say what he disliked, and Fats often agreed and recut it.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Were these long sessions, then, I mean with all this arguing and everything going on?
Oh my God, yeah.
You din't get through them easy.
NO, of course you start, what, supposed to be four hour, four to five hours, and we did more than that quite often, you know. And --
Most of it spent arguing?
No, I wouldn't say that. No, because you got to rehearse the tune, keep going over it to make a record before we're happy.
Oh, I see.

See, and before he's happy, and he say let's try it like that, and bang (snaps fingers) the guys would jump up like -- the engineers, and record! Record! Beautiful. Beautiful! Don't touch it. Don't touch it! And sometimes Fats would say -- he would look at me, you know (laughs). I hate like hell to take this credit, but I mean I

bugged him. Well, maybe I did, and I -- if I didn't like something, and I thought it was going to endanger him, or us, down the line somewhere, I'd get his eye and say, you know, kind of shake my head a little.
I see.
You know? Because I -- maybe I saw something he didn't see, or maybe I thought he didn't hear, and he thought the same.
When you speak of endangering Fats, what do you mean? What kind of thing -- I mean session would endanger him?

Well, oh I mean should you record something, you record something, and it didn't turn out to be so right, and I'd tell you later, and you'd say well why didn't you tell me? Why didn't you call it to my attention? That's why I hired you, because I liked the way you think, and the way you hear, and the way you play, and you may tell me then, I kind of depend on you when we do something, if it isn't right I figure you will help -- you will tell me, or call it to my attention. You know?

Because nobody's perfect, after all, you know. I mean I'm not telling you, I just said it. And now looking -- then he'd -- okay, take five, and wander down there, and we'd take a walk and go to the john, which was way down around the hall somewhere. I wouldn't dare say anything to him about
this situation, in front of the guys, you know, I wouldn't dare, you know.
I see, so this was when you took your walk.

Yeah, he and I, nobody but he went, you know, just he and I would know what expired, what went on, you know? After we get out he say what's the matter? I say I don't think you want that. Why? You know. I says such and such. He say yeah? No wonder. Thanks. You know. A lot of times he's told me that.

I've had a lot of times he's told me, say Hermie, come-here I'd say what? "Get in there with the plunger." But I didn't think much of the idea, maybe, anyway. Or I would use it to the best of my ability. I thought. And so -- and I would ask him to take it out. I didn't want to tell him right in front of the guys, I don't like that. You should take it out. And he'd say damn, this guy ain't going to run the session, you know what happens in those --

So I'd take him aside, and I'd explain to him what I thought, and we would compare notes, he said you-see, well all right, now that you mention it, I think you're right. Or I don't think you're right. Keep it in. Or whatever. You know. And then I would say well if I were you I wouldn't do this here. I would have done it earlier, or not at all, or something, you know, and then we'd go back. He'd say cut another one.
And he'd say okay, instead of coming in such a place, you do this, and you do that, and so and so.

Ah, that is better, Fats, maybe they would say, or we'll keep both of them, see. Now they would do this, and they would do -- maybe they'd sell both of them, but you still had two we had left, see? Uh-huh?
